author: Adria Goins/KFOR
title: Edmond infant hears for the first time through hearing device - NewsBreak
text:
By Adria Goins/KFOR ,
9 hours ago
OKLAHOMA CITY ( KFOR ) – It will be a holiday season to remember for one Edmond family. Their 11-month-old daughter experienced the gift of sound for the first time when her cochlear implant was turned on during a screening at Hearts for Hearing on Wednesday.
The family of Olivia Butler-Thomas started filing into a room at the non-profit’s location off Portland in Oklahoma City. There were about a dozen of them, all excited and a little nervous about the big day.
“Just an emotional roller coaster, really, more than anything,” said Kim Butler-Thomas, Olivia’s mother.
First, while Olivia was distracted by her family, crews with Hearts for Hearing started testing the device by sending beeping sounds to the implant. They were checking to see if it was working properly. After the tests were complete, it was time for the big moment.
A family member said her name. Olivia turned to the sound. The baby girl was hearing her family’s voices and noises for the first time.
“Really just a dream come true to see her have full access to sound. When we first learned that she had profound hearing loss, it was quite devastating for our family,” said Mandy Butler-Thomas, Olivia’s mother.
Holiday hazards ahead of Thanksgiving Her parents were told she suffered from hearing loss shortly after the little girl was born. After research and long conversations, the family made the decision to install cochlear implants.
“Going through this journey and going through, you know, two surgeries and seeing her react to sound and learn her name and turn to sound has just been amazing to see,” said Mandy.
Sophia Banos has been the infant’s speech language pathologist for the last six months and helped to activate her left-ear implant a few weeks earlier. Banos was there to turn on the right-ear device on Wednesday.
“Now she’ll be able to tell which side sound is coming from and be able to use both of her ears to just perceive the world around her,” said Banos.
It was a beautiful moment that was worth the wait and fears for Olivia’s family.
“More happy tears than sad tears these days,” said Kim.
Hearts for Hearing is a non-profit organization that provides the family with the devices at no cost.
